notes: Раздел 2.1 называет ИС Univer / Moodle; раздел 2.3.2 предписывает проведение экзамена в ИС Univer. Оба указания сохранены.
Программа не задаёт число вариантов и правильных ответов. Пять вариантов и один правильный ответ выбраны для данного учебного банка.
Короткие тексты и диалоги оригинальные, не заимствованы из упражнений учебников.
Аудирование и устное произношение не проверяются без аудиоматериалов; имеются текстовые задания по фонетике.

topics.name: 1A All about you — questions, common verb phrases, alphabet
1B Describing people — present simple, appearance, personality, -s/-es
1C Art comes to life — present continuous, clothes, place, /ʃ/ and /ʒ/
2A Lost and found — past simple, holidays
2B On top of the world — past continuous, at/in/on, weak forms
2C A story to remember — sequencers, connectors, verb phrases, stress
3A The waiting game — be going to, airports, letter g
3B Can we meet? — future arrangements, verb + preposition
3C Word games — defining relative clauses, paraphrasing, silent e
4A Have you finished yet? — present perfect, housework, make/do
4B Shopping — present perfect vs past simple, functional language, reading
5B Cities — superlatives, quantifiers, towns, health and body
5C Too much or not enough? — will/won’t, opposite verbs, back

notes: Все вопросы имеют один правильный ответ из пяти.
Уровни сложности являются авторской оценкой; официальное распределение сложности не заявляется.
Содержание привязано ко всем 15 неделям программы 2026 года. Вопросы и пояснения представлены на английском языке.

questions.question: Choose the correct question about Ali's home.

questions.question: Complete: What ___ your first name?
questions.explanation: The singular subject your first name takes is.

questions.question: Choose the correct question about Sara's job.
questions.explanation: Use does before the singular subject and do as the main verb.

questions.question: Complete: ___ brothers have you got?
questions.explanation: Brothers is a plural countable noun.

questions.question: Choose the question that asks about a class start time.
questions.explanation: What time asks for a clock time.

options.text: Why do you like the class?
What time does the class start?

questions.question: Choose the correct subject question.
questions.explanation: Who as the subject does not need does in this question.

questions.question: Put the words into a standard yes/no question: can / you / spell / it.
questions.explanation: A standard modal question puts can before the subject.

questions.question: Complete: ___ you like studying in the library?
questions.explanation: Use do to ask about a present simple action with you.

questions.question: Which question asks about frequency?
questions.explanation: How often asks about frequency.

questions.question: Complete: ___ notebook is this? — It is Dana's.
questions.explanation: Whose asks about possession.

questions.question: Complete: ___ is this dictionary? — Twelve pounds.
questions.explanation: How much asks about price.

questions.question: Complete: How ___ are you? — I am nineteen.
questions.explanation: How old asks about age.

questions.question: Choose the correct request when you do not know the letters in a name.
questions.explanation: Spell asks for the letters of a word.

options.text: How do you spell your surname?
When do you wear your surname?

questions.question: Complete the common phrase: ___ up at seven in the morning.
questions.explanation: Get up means leave your bed after sleeping.

questions.question: Complete the phrase: go ___ bed.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is go to bed.

questions.question: Complete: I usually ___ my homework after dinner.
questions.explanation: The usual collocation is do homework.

questions.question: Complete: We ___ breakfast at eight.
questions.explanation: Have breakfast means eat the morning meal.

questions.question: Complete: Can you ___ a photo of us?
questions.explanation: The collocation is take a photo.

questions.question: Complete: I listen ___ music on the bus.
questions.explanation: Listen is followed by to before the object.

questions.question: Complete: My sister works ___ a nurse.
questions.explanation: Work as introduces a person's job.

questions.question: Which letter name is pronounced /eɪ/ in English?
questions.explanation: The letter A is pronounced /eɪ/.

questions.question: Which letter name is pronounced /juː/ in English?
questions.explanation: The letter U has the name /juː/.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate answer: Where are you from?
questions.explanation: The question asks about origin.

questions.question: Read: My name is Lina. I study biology and share a flat with my cousin. Who lives with Lina?
questions.explanation: The text says she shares a flat with her cousin.

questions.question: Choose the question that matches this answer. “I’m looking for my student card.”
questions.explanation: In a direct question, are comes before you. The verb phrase is look for.

options.text: What do you look for yesterday?

questions.question: A new student says, “I got here on the number 14 bus.” Which question is she answering?
questions.explanation: The bus tells us how she travelled.

questions.question: Complete the question. “Which language ___ at home, Aida?”
questions.explanation: Use do + subject + base verb for this present simple question.

questions.question: At registration, the tutor wants to know which class a student is in. Which question should she ask?
questions.explanation: Which group asks for the group name or number.

questions.question: Complete the usual verb phrase. “I always ___ a shower after basketball practice.”
questions.explanation: Have a shower is a common phrase in British English.

questions.question: Which set of letters is read “ess, double-u, jay”?
questions.explanation: These are the English names of S, W and J, in order.

questions.question: A club form asks for your “surname”, but you are unsure what the word means. Which question will help?
questions.explanation: What does a word mean? is the standard way to ask about its meaning.

options.text: Where does a surname go to?

questions.question: Complete: My brother ___ in a bank.
questions.explanation: Use the -s form with a third-person singular subject.

questions.question: Complete: We ___ near the university.
questions.explanation: Use the base form with we in the present simple.

questions.question: Complete: Eva ___ coffee; she prefers tea.
questions.explanation: After doesn't, use the base form drink.

questions.question: Complete: ___ your parents work on Saturdays?
questions.explanation: Use do with the plural subject your parents.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: Present simple third-person singular needs walks.

options.text: He does usually walks to work.
He walks usually to work does.

questions.question: Complete: My teacher is ___ late; she always arrives early.
questions.explanation: Never fits the meaning of arriving early every time.

questions.question: Complete: How often ___ she visit her grandparents?
questions.explanation: Use does with she in a present simple question.

questions.question: Choose the correct short answer: Does Mark like chess?
questions.explanation: Match the auxiliary does in the question.

questions.question: Complete: The shop ___ at nine every weekday.
questions.explanation: A regular schedule can use the present simple.

questions.question: Complete: I ___ wear a tie to my classes.
questions.explanation: Use don't with I before a base verb.

questions.question: Choose the correct negative sentence.
questions.explanation: Doesn't is followed by the base form drive.

questions.question: Complete: ___ does your uncle do? — He is a chef.
questions.explanation: What does someone do asks about their job.

questions.question: Complete: The students ___ English twice a week.
questions.explanation: A plural subject takes study.

questions.question: Read: Omar cycles to college from Monday to Friday. He takes the bus on Saturday. How does he travel on weekdays?
questions.explanation: Monday to Friday are weekdays, when Omar cycles.

questions.question: A person who likes giving things to other people is ___.
questions.explanation: Generous describes willingness to give or share.

questions.question: A person who does not like doing much work is ___.
questions.explanation: Lazy means unwilling to work or make an effort.

questions.question: A person who finds it difficult to talk to strangers may be ___.
questions.explanation: Shy describes nervousness in social situations.

questions.question: Someone who tells the truth is ___.
questions.explanation: Honest describes truthful behaviour.

questions.question: Complete: My sister has long, ___ hair, with no curls.
questions.explanation: Straight hair does not have curls.

questions.question: Which question asks about appearance rather than personality?
questions.explanation: Look like asks about physical appearance.

options.text: What is he like as a person?

questions.question: Which question asks about someone's character?
questions.explanation: Be like can ask for a description of personality.

options.text: What is your new flatmate like?

questions.question: In which word is the final -s pronounced /s/?
questions.explanation: After the voiceless /k/, the ending is /s/.

questions.question: In which word is the final -s pronounced /ɪz/?
questions.explanation: After /tʃ/, the ending adds the syllable /ɪz/.

questions.question: Choose the best reply: What is your new classmate like? — He is very ___. He always says please and thank you.
questions.explanation: The behaviour described is polite.

questions.question: Complete the sentence about a regular habit. “On Fridays, Sam ___ his brother to school.”
questions.explanation: With he or she, change a consonant + y to -ies in carries.

questions.question: Choose the correct reply. “Do your neighbours work from home?” “Yes, ___.”
questions.explanation: The subject is plural, and the short answer repeats do.

questions.question: “Jamil likes meeting new people and starts conversations easily.” Which word describes him best?
questions.explanation: An outgoing person enjoys meeting people and talking to them.

questions.question: Which phrase describes physical appearance?
questions.explanation: Hair length and shape are details of appearance.

questions.question: Choose the sentence that asks about frequency.
questions.explanation: How often asks how frequently something happens.

options.text: How many stops does the bus have?
How far does Dina walk to the bus stop?
How long does the bus ride take?
How much is Dina’s bus ticket?
How often does Dina miss the bus?

questions.question: What do the present simple forms “fixes” and “misses” have in common?
questions.explanation: Fix ends in /ks/ and miss ends in /s/. Adding -es gives an extra /ɪz/ syllable.

options.text: Both endings are pronounced /z/ with no extra syllable.
Each gains an extra syllable pronounced /ɪz/.
Both endings are pronounced /s/ with no extra syllable.
Both words lose their final consonant.

questions.question: Read the profile. “Liam rarely speaks in large meetings. In small groups, he listens carefully and makes sure everyone has a turn.” Which description fits the second sentence?
questions.explanation: He thinks about other people’s needs and gives them time to speak.

questions.question: Complete: Look! The children ___ in the garden.
questions.explanation: Present continuous uses are + -ing with a plural subject.

questions.question: Complete: I ___ a blue jacket today.
questions.explanation: Use am + wearing with I.

questions.question: Complete: Please be quiet. The baby ___.
questions.explanation: Use is + -ing for an action in progress.

questions.question: Choose the correct question.
questions.explanation: Present continuous questions put are before you.

questions.question: Choose the correct negative sentence about watching television now.
questions.explanation: Use aren't + -ing with they.

questions.question: Complete: At the moment, Leo ___ an email.
questions.explanation: At the moment identifies an action in progress.

questions.question: Complete: The two artists ___ a wall right now.
questions.explanation: A plural subject takes are painting.

questions.question: Choose the correct -ing form of run.
questions.explanation: Double the final n before adding -ing.

questions.question: Choose the correct -ing form of make.
questions.explanation: Drop the silent final e before adding -ing.

questions.question: Complete: She usually wears trainers, but today she ___ boots.
questions.explanation: Today contrasts a temporary action with her usual habit.

questions.question: Complete the short answer: Is Dad cooking? — No, ___.
questions.explanation: Use the negative form of is in the answer.

questions.question: Complete: Why ___ you laughing?
questions.explanation: The continuous question uses are with you.

questions.question: Which item do you usually wear on your feet inside your shoes?
questions.explanation: Socks are worn on the feet.

questions.question: Which item is usually worn around the neck to keep warm?
questions.explanation: A scarf can protect the neck from cold.

questions.question: Which item is usually worn on the hands in cold weather?
questions.explanation: Gloves cover the hands.

questions.question: Complete: There is a black cat ___ the table, so its head is below the tabletop.
questions.explanation: Under expresses a lower position beneath something.

questions.question: Complete: The painting is ___ the sofa, higher on the wall.
questions.explanation: Above means in a higher position.

questions.question: Complete: The small shop is ___ the bank and the café.
questions.explanation: Between relates one object to two others.

questions.question: Complete: Sit ___ me; the chair next to mine is empty.
questions.explanation: Beside means next to.

questions.question: Which word contains the sound /ʃ/?
questions.explanation: The initial sound in shoe is /ʃ/.

questions.question: Which word contains the sound /ʒ/?
questions.explanation: Television contains the voiced sound /ʒ/.

questions.question: Read: In the picture, a woman is holding a red bag. A child beside her is drawing. Who has the bag?
questions.explanation: The text identifies the woman as the person holding the bag.

questions.question: Choose the best answer: What are you wearing for the photo today?
questions.explanation: The question asks about clothes being worn today.

options.text: A white shirt and black trousers.
My brother took it last year.
I usually get up at seven.
The photo is on the wall.

questions.question: Read: It is raining. Dan is standing under a tree, and his bike is behind him. Where is the bike?
questions.explanation: The text states that the bike is behind him.

questions.question: Complete the live description. “In the studio right now, the artist ___ a portrait.”
questions.explanation: An action happening now uses is + the -ing form with the artist.

questions.question: Two children are standing in front of a glass case. Where is the glass case in relation to them?
questions.explanation: If the children are in front of the case, it is behind them.

questions.question: What do you usually fasten around your waist to keep trousers in place?
questions.explanation: A belt goes around the waist and holds trousers up.

questions.question: In which word can you hear /ʒ/ as in the middle of “vision”?
questions.explanation: Measure contains /ʒ/. The other words contain /ʃ/.

questions.question: Complete the description. “The visitors ___ their coats now because the room is warm.”
questions.explanation: Use are + the -ing form for an action in progress with a plural subject.

questions.question: “The notice is fixed to the surface of the door.” Which phrase means the same thing?
questions.explanation: On indicates contact with a surface.

questions.question: A museum livestream shows change in progress. The model still has one boot in her hand. Which sentence fits the scene?
questions.explanation: Is putting on describes the action that is still happening.

options.text: She is putting on her boots.
She took her boots off last night.
She puts on boots for work every week.

questions.question: Complete in the past simple: We ___ a museum yesterday.
questions.explanation: The regular past simple form is visited.

questions.question: Choose the past simple of go.
questions.explanation: Go has the irregular past form went.

questions.question: Choose the past simple of buy.
questions.explanation: The irregular past form of buy is bought.

questions.question: Complete in the past simple: I ___ my phone on the bus last night.
questions.explanation: The past simple of lose is lost.

questions.question: Complete: Did you ___ your passport?
questions.explanation: After did, use the base form.

questions.question: Choose the correct past simple negative.
questions.explanation: Didn't takes a base verb.

options.text: We not stayed in a hotel.
We weren't stay in a hotel.
We didn't stayed in a hotel.
We don't stayed in a hotel.
We didn't stay in a hotel.

questions.question: Complete: Where ___ you go on holiday last summer?
questions.explanation: Last summer requires a past question with did.

questions.question: Complete: The tickets ___ expensive last year.
questions.explanation: The plural subject tickets takes were in the past.

questions.question: Complete: The weather ___ sunny on our first day.
questions.explanation: The singular noun weather takes was.

questions.question: Choose the correct past question.
questions.explanation: Use did before the subject and the base form land.

questions.question: Choose the past simple of take.
questions.explanation: Take has the irregular past form took.

questions.question: Complete in the past simple: Nora ___ her friend at the station.
questions.explanation: The past form of meet is met.

questions.question: Complete: Did they enjoy the trip? — Yes, they ___.
questions.explanation: The short answer repeats did.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelled past simple form of study.
questions.explanation: Consonant + y changes to -ied.

questions.question: Complete the holiday phrase: ___ sightseeing.
questions.explanation: Go sightseeing is the usual phrase.

questions.question: Where can travellers sleep in a tent?
questions.explanation: A campsite provides places for tents.

questions.question: What do you usually need to cross an international border as a traveller?
questions.explanation: A passport is a travel identity document.

questions.question: What do you call the bags you take on a journey?
questions.explanation: Luggage refers to travellers' bags.

questions.question: Complete: We booked our ___ at a small guest house.
questions.explanation: Accommodation means a place to stay.

questions.question: Complete: We ___ a car so we could drive around the island.
questions.explanation: Hire a car means pay to use it temporarily.

questions.question: Which phrase means spend time lying outside in the sun?
questions.explanation: Sunbathe describes relaxing in sunlight.

questions.question: Read: Ben left his camera in a café. The waiter found it and called him. Who found the camera?
questions.explanation: The waiter is explicitly named as the finder.

questions.question: Read: Our flight was cancelled, so we travelled by train instead. How did we finally travel?
questions.explanation: The flight did not operate, and the travellers took a train.

questions.question: Read: We stayed for two nights in Astana and then three nights in Almaty. Where did we stay longer?
questions.explanation: Three nights is longer than two.

questions.question: Complete the sentence. “We ___ the first train yesterday because our alarm didn’t ring.”
questions.explanation: Yesterday places the event in the past. Miss is regular, so its past form is missed.

questions.question: Complete the question. “Where did you ___ your cabin key?”
questions.explanation: After did, use the base form leave.

questions.question: “The forecast was bad, so the guide ___ us back to the hotel.” Choose the past form of bring.
questions.explanation: Brought is the irregular past form of bring.

questions.question: What do you usually do at reception when you arrive at a hotel and want your room key?
questions.explanation: When you check in at a hotel, you register your arrival and get access to your room.

questions.question: “We spent the morning looking around the old town and its famous buildings.” Which activity does this describe?
questions.explanation: Sightseeing means visiting interesting places, often while travelling.

questions.question: Which question asks how long a past holiday lasted?
questions.explanation: How many days asks for the duration.

options.text: How much did the hotel cost?
How far was it from home?
How many people went with you?
How many days did you spend there?
What time did you get back?

questions.question: Read the note. “We were going to rent bikes on Sunday. The shop was closed, so we walked to the lake instead.” What did they actually do?
questions.explanation: The final sentence says that they walked instead of renting bikes.

options.text: They visited the lake on Saturday.

questions.question: Complete in the past continuous: At eight yesterday, I ___ dinner.
questions.explanation: I takes was + -ing.

questions.question: Complete: They ___ football when the rain started.
questions.explanation: They takes were + -ing.

questions.question: Choose the correct past continuous question.
questions.explanation: Use were + subject + -ing.

questions.question: Choose the correct negative.
questions.explanation: Use wasn't + -ing with she.

options.text: She wasn't listen when I spoke.
She wasn't listening when I spoke.
She weren't listening when I spoke.
She didn't listening when I spoke.
She not listening when I spoke.

questions.question: Complete: While I ___, the lights went out.
questions.explanation: The ongoing past action is expressed by was reading.

questions.question: Complete: He ___ his arm while he was skiing.
questions.explanation: The completed event interrupting the background activity takes past simple.

questions.question: Complete: We were walking home when it ___ to snow.
questions.explanation: The new event is expressed by past simple.

questions.question: Choose the past continuous form of sit with she.
questions.explanation: Double t in sitting and use was with she.

questions.question: Complete: What ___ Tom doing when you saw him?
questions.explanation: Use was with singular Tom in the past continuous.

questions.question: Complete the short answer: Were the children studying? — No, they ___.
questions.explanation: The answer repeats were in its negative form.

questions.question: Read: At ten, Maya was studying and her brother was washing the dishes. What was her brother doing?
questions.explanation: The text names his ongoing activity.

questions.question: Which sentence describes an action already in progress at a past moment?
questions.explanation: Was waiting marks an ongoing past action.

options.text: At six, I was waiting outside.

questions.question: Complete: I ___ a shower when the phone rang.
questions.explanation: Use past continuous for the interrupted activity.

questions.question: Choose the sentence describing two simultaneous ongoing past actions.
questions.explanation: The two past continuous actions overlap.

options.text: I cook and Eva sets the table every day.
I have cooked and Eva has left.
While I was cooking, Eva was setting the table.
I will cook when Eva arrives.

questions.question: Complete: Our class starts ___ nine o'clock.
questions.explanation: Use at with a clock time.

questions.question: Complete: My birthday is ___ October.
questions.explanation: Use in with months.

questions.question: Complete: The meeting is ___ Monday.
questions.explanation: Use on with days.

questions.question: Complete: She was born ___ 2007.
questions.explanation: Use in with years.

questions.question: Complete: We usually study ___ the evening.
questions.explanation: The phrase is in the evening.

questions.question: Complete: Many people sleep ___ night.
questions.explanation: The usual phrase is at night.

questions.question: Complete: The keys are ___ my bag, inside its front pocket.
questions.explanation: In describes an enclosed location.

questions.question: Complete: We met ___ the bus stop, at the place where the bus collects passengers.
questions.explanation: At identifies a point or meeting location.

questions.question: Complete: The photo is hanging ___ the wall.
questions.explanation: Use on for attachment to a wall.

questions.question: In unstressed British pronunciation, which is a common weak form of were?
questions.explanation: Were commonly has the weak form /wə/ when unstressed.

questions.question: Complete the sentence. “At half past seven yesterday, Farida and I ___ for a map at the station.”
questions.explanation: The subject Farida and I takes were. The -ing form describes the activity in progress.

questions.question: “While the hotel staff were serving breakfast, the lights suddenly ___ out.”
questions.explanation: Use the past simple went for the sudden event during another action.

questions.question: Complete the sentence about a date. “The photo was taken ___ 14 September.”
questions.explanation: Use on before a specific date.

questions.question: Which phrase completes the usual time expression? “The streets were empty ___ the early morning, around five.”
questions.explanation: The usual expression is in the early morning.

questions.question: In standard British English, which is the usual weak form of “was” in an unstressed sentence such as “I was waiting”?
questions.explanation: Unstressed was commonly has the schwa /ə/ and keeps the final /z/.

questions.question: Choose the best answer to “What were they doing when the bus arrived?”
questions.explanation: The question asks about the action already in progress at that past moment.

options.text: They were looking at the timetable.
They have a map in their bag.

questions.question: Read the message. “At nine, Lena was crossing the bridge. As she was crossing, her phone rang.” Which event interrupted the other activity?
questions.explanation: The phone rang during the longer activity of crossing the bridge.

options.text: She reached the far side of the bridge.

questions.question: Complete: ___, I packed my bag. Then I called a taxi.
questions.explanation: First introduces the first step of a sequence.

questions.question: Complete: We checked in. ___, we went through security.
questions.explanation: Then introduces the next event.

questions.question: Complete: We waited for two hours. ___, the bus arrived.
questions.explanation: Finally introduces the last or long-awaited event.

questions.question: Complete: I stayed at home ___ I felt ill.
questions.explanation: Because introduces the reason.

questions.question: Complete: It was raining, ___ we took an umbrella.
questions.explanation: So introduces the result.

questions.question: Complete: The room was small, ___ it was comfortable.
questions.explanation: But introduces a contrast.

questions.question: Complete: ___ it was cold, we enjoyed the walk.
questions.explanation: Although introduces a contrast with the main clause.

questions.question: Complete: I washed my hands ___ I ate the sandwich.
questions.explanation: Before places one action earlier than another.

questions.question: Complete: ___ dinner, we went for a short walk.
questions.explanation: After can be followed directly by the noun dinner.

questions.question: Read: I missed the bus because I got up late. Why did I miss the bus?
questions.explanation: The reason is explicitly given after because.

questions.question: Read: First we bought tickets. Then we found our seats. Finally the film began. What happened second?
questions.explanation: Then marks the second event.

questions.question: Read: I was tired, but I finished the report. Did I finish it?
questions.explanation: But contrasts tiredness with completing the report.

options.text: The text says I never started.
Only after my friend finished it.

questions.question: Read: The train left before we reached the station. Which happened first?
questions.explanation: Before places the departure earlier than the arrival.

options.text: We bought food at the station.

questions.question: Read: Anna dropped her keys. A boy picked them up and gave them back. Who returned the keys?
questions.explanation: The boy picked up and returned the keys.

questions.question: Read: I could not open the door, so I called my flatmate. What was the result of the problem?
questions.explanation: So introduces the resulting action.

questions.question: Complete the phrase: ___ a mistake.
questions.explanation: The collocation is make a mistake.

questions.question: Complete the phrase: ___ the bus to college.
questions.explanation: Take the bus means travel by bus.

questions.question: Complete: Please ___ me a call when you arrive.
questions.explanation: The phrase is give someone a call.

questions.question: Complete: We ___ a great time at the festival.
questions.explanation: Have a great time means enjoy yourself.

questions.question: Complete: I ___ my keys, so I could not get into the flat.
questions.explanation: Lost fits the consequence of being unable to enter.

questions.question: In the word holiday, which syllable normally has primary stress?
questions.explanation: Holiday is normally stressed on its first syllable.

questions.question: In the word remember, which syllable has primary stress?
questions.explanation: Remember is stressed on the second syllable.

questions.question: Which word has primary stress on its second syllable?
questions.explanation: Begin is stressed on the second syllable.

questions.question: “We stopped for water ___ we continued walking.” Which word shows that the stop came first?
questions.explanation: Before places the stop earlier than the next action.

questions.question: “The room was quiet ___ everyone could hear a clock in the hall.” Choose the connector that introduces the result.
questions.explanation: So introduces what happened as a result of the room being quiet.

questions.question: Complete the usual phrase. “The driver slowed down to ___ a look at the sign.”
questions.explanation: Take a look means to look at something, often briefly.

questions.question: Which word has the main stress on the first syllable?
questions.explanation: In picnic, the first syllable is stressed.

questions.question: Choose the connector. “___ Noor felt nervous, she went on stage and finished her speech.”
questions.explanation: Although links an unexpected contrast: she went on stage despite feeling nervous.

questions.question: Read the notes. “First, we reached the campsite. Before putting up the tent, we phoned the owner. We cooked after the tent was ready.” Which action came immediately before they put up the tent?
questions.explanation: Before putting up the tent, they phoned the owner.

questions.question: Read the story. “Mira missed her stop because she fell asleep. When she got off, she called her friend, who met her outside the station.” Why did Mira miss her stop?
questions.explanation: Because introduces the reason she missed her stop.

options.text: She called her friend too early.
She wanted to buy a ticket.

questions.question: Complete with be going to: I ___ study tonight.
questions.explanation: Use am going to with I.

questions.question: Complete with be going to: They ___ visit their aunt.
questions.explanation: Use are going to with they.

questions.question: Complete: She is going to ___ a new course.
questions.explanation: Going to is followed by a base verb.

questions.question: Choose the correct question about a plan to travel alone.
questions.explanation: Put are before the subject in this question.

options.text: Is you going to travel alone?

questions.question: Read the message. “I looked everywhere for my gloves. Nobody at the pool had seen them. When I came home, I found one of my gloves on each of the two kitchen chairs.” What do we learn at the end?
questions.explanation: She found both of her gloves, one on each of the two chairs.

options.text: The gloves were left in a café.
The pool staff found both gloves.
At least one glove was still at the pool.
She decided to buy new gloves.

questions.question: Complete: My new bag is ___ than my old one.
questions.explanation: Use the comparative bigger with than.

questions.question: Complete: This exercise is ___ than the last one.
questions.explanation: Easy changes to easier in the comparative.

questions.question: Complete: This course is ___ than that short workshop.
questions.explanation: Longer adjectives commonly use more in the comparative.

questions.question: Choose the comparative of good.
questions.explanation: Good has the irregular comparative better.

questions.question: Choose the comparative of bad.
questions.explanation: Bad has the irregular comparative worse.

questions.question: Complete: A bicycle is usually cheaper ___ a car.
questions.explanation: Than introduces the second part of a comparison.

questions.question: Complete: My brother drives ___ than I do.
questions.explanation: Use the comparative adverb more carefully to describe drives.

questions.question: Complete: Please speak ___; I can't follow you.
questions.explanation: More slowly is the comparative of slowly.

questions.question: Complete: Amina runs ___ than her cousin.
questions.explanation: Fast has the comparative form faster.

questions.question: Complete: The second question is not as difficult ___ the first.
questions.explanation: Use as ... as for this comparison pattern.

questions.question: Choose the correct comparison of the warmth of two rooms.
questions.explanation: Much can strengthen a comparative, but more warmer is a double comparative.

options.text: This room is more warmer than that one.
This room is much warmer than that one.
This room is much warmest than that one.
This room is most warmer than that one.
This room is warm than that one.

questions.question: Read: The train takes two hours and the bus takes three. Which is faster on this route?
questions.explanation: The train takes less time.

questions.question: Read: Box A weighs 4 kg and Box B weighs 7 kg. Which statement is true?
questions.explanation: Seven kilograms is heavier than four.

options.text: Box B is lighter than Box A.
Box B is heavier than Box A.
Box A is heavier than Box B.

questions.question: Read: Noor types 50 words a minute and Asel types 60. Who types more quickly?
questions.explanation: Asel types more words in the same time.

questions.question: Choose the correct comparative of happy.
questions.explanation: Change y to i before -er.

questions.question: Choose the comparative of little when it refers to amount.
questions.explanation: Less is the comparative for a smaller amount.

questions.question: How do you read 21 as an ordinal number?
questions.explanation: The ordinal form is twenty-first.

questions.question: How do you read 50%?
questions.explanation: 50% is fifty per cent.

questions.question: Which expression means 1/2?
questions.explanation: A half is one of two equal parts.

questions.question: Which number is written one thousand two hundred?
questions.explanation: One thousand plus two hundred is 1,200.

questions.question: Read: A laptop costs £600 and a tablet costs £450. How much more expensive is the laptop?
questions.explanation: Subtract 450 from 600.

questions.question: Read: Route A is 8 km and takes 40 minutes. Route B is 10 km and takes 30 minutes. Which description is correct?
questions.explanation: Route B has more kilometres but fewer minutes.

options.text: Route B is shorter and slower.
Both routes are the same length.
Route A is longer and quicker.
Route B is longer but quicker.

questions.question: Read: Kim is 160 cm tall, Eva is 165 cm and Lina is 170 cm. Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: Eva's height lies between the other two.

options.text: Eva is taller than Kim but shorter than Lina.

questions.question: Complete the comparison. “A message by email reaches us ___ than a letter by post.”
questions.explanation: Soon has the comparative form sooner, used before than.

questions.question: Complete the comparison. “This backpack is ___ than mine. It weighs only half as much.”
questions.explanation: Use lighter to compare the lower weight of one backpack with another.

questions.question: “Leo scored 84 per cent and Mia scored 72 per cent.” Which statement is true?
questions.explanation: Eighty-four is greater than seventy-two.

options.text: Mia scored more than 84 per cent.
Leo’s score was higher than Mia’s.
Mia’s score was higher than Leo’s.

questions.question: Choose the correct way to read the fraction ¾.
questions.explanation: In the fraction ¾, three of four equal parts are counted.

questions.question: Choose the correct way to read this phone-number segment digit by digit: 604.
questions.explanation: Read each digit individually in the order shown.

questions.question: One parcel weighs exactly 2 kg and a second parcel weighs exactly 2 kg. Which comparison is accurate?
questions.explanation: As heavy as describes equal weight.

options.text: The first parcel is less heavy than the second.
The second parcel is twice as heavy.
The second parcel is lighter than the first.
The first parcel is as heavy as the second.
The first parcel is heavier than the second.

questions.question: Complete: This is ___ building in our town.
questions.explanation: Use the + superlative tallest.

questions.question: Choose the superlative of good.
questions.explanation: Best is the irregular superlative.

questions.question: Complete: It is ___ interesting museum I have visited.
questions.explanation: Use the most with the superlative of interesting.

questions.question: Choose the superlative of bad.
questions.explanation: Worst is the irregular superlative.

questions.question: Complete: Of the three hotels, this one is ___.
questions.explanation: Use a superlative when comparing one item with the whole group.

questions.question: Read: Lake A is 20 m deep, Lake B is 50 m and Lake C is 35 m. Which is the deepest?
questions.explanation: Lake B has the greatest depth.

questions.question: Complete: There are ___ cars in the centre; the streets are crowded.
questions.explanation: Cars is countable and plural, so use too many.

questions.question: Complete: There is ___ traffic today. We are moving very slowly.
questions.explanation: Traffic is uncountable, so use too much.

questions.question: Complete: We have ___ time, so we can walk instead of taking a taxi.
questions.explanation: Enough time means sufficient time.

questions.question: Complete: There isn't ___ milk for three cups of tea.
questions.explanation: Enough can modify uncountable milk.

questions.question: Complete: I have ___ close friends — just two or three.
questions.explanation: A few is used with plural countable friends.

questions.question: Complete: Add ___ water, about a spoonful.
questions.explanation: A little is used with uncountable water.

questions.question: Complete: There is very ___ space in this lift, so we cannot all get in.
questions.explanation: Space is uncountable in this context.

questions.question: Which part of the body connects your head to your shoulders?
questions.explanation: The neck connects the head and trunk.

questions.question: Which joint is between the upper and lower parts of the leg?
questions.explanation: The knee is the leg joint named in the question.

questions.question: Complete: I can't talk loudly because I have a sore ___.
questions.explanation: A sore throat can make speaking uncomfortable.

questions.question: Which body part do you normally use to smell?
questions.explanation: The nose is associated with the sense of smell.

questions.question: A town with little noise is ___.
questions.explanation: Quiet describes a low level of noise.

questions.question: A city with many people in a small space is ___.
questions.explanation: Crowded means full of people.

questions.question: Complete: There ___ a hospital next to the station.
questions.explanation: Use there is with a singular noun.

questions.question: Complete: There ___ two parks near my home.
questions.explanation: Use there are with a plural noun.

questions.question: Complete: ___ there a pharmacy near here?
questions.explanation: Invert is in the question with a singular noun.

questions.question: Read: Town X has three parks and little traffic. Town Y has no parks and heavy traffic. Which statement is supported?
questions.explanation: The comparison follows both pieces of information.

options.text: Town X has more parks and less traffic.

questions.question: Complete the sentence. “Of the three streets, Mill Street is ___ in the evening. Hardly any cars use it.” Choose the superlative of quiet.
questions.explanation: Hardly any cars suggests the street is quiet, and the superlative compares all three.

questions.question: Complete the sentence about a café. “There aren’t ___ clean cups for all twelve guests. We need to wash three more.”
questions.explanation: Enough means as many as are needed.

questions.question: A visitor needs a printed map and advice about local attractions. Which place is set up to provide both?
questions.explanation: A tourist information centre provides visitors with maps and advice on local sights.

questions.question: Which body part connects the hand to the forearm?
questions.explanation: The wrist is the joint between the hand and the forearm.

questions.question: Complete the sentence about a small amount of an uncountable noun. “Put ___ water in the glass, just a small amount.”
questions.explanation: Use a little with an uncountable noun such as water.

questions.question: Read the options. “Central Clinic: 10 min by bus. North Clinic: 18 min by bus. Park Clinic: 15 min by bus.” Which clinic is quickest to reach by bus?
questions.explanation: Ten minutes is the shortest of the three journey times.

options.text: All three take the same time
North and Park take the same time

questions.question: Complete: I think it ___ rain tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Will is followed directly by a base verb.

questions.question: Choose the correct negative form of will.
questions.explanation: Won't is the standard contraction of will not.

questions.question: Complete: Don't worry. I ___ help you with the bags.
questions.explanation: Will can introduce an offer of help.

questions.question: Complete: She will ___ you after the lesson.
questions.explanation: Use the base form after will.

questions.question: Choose the correct future question about being at home tonight.
questions.explanation: Put will before the subject and use be.

options.text: Are you will at home tonight?
Will you to be at home tonight?
Will you be at home tonight?
Do you will be at home tonight?
Will be you at home tonight?

questions.question: Complete: Will they come? — Yes, they ___.
questions.explanation: The short answer repeats will.

questions.question: Complete: Will it snow? — No, it ___.
questions.explanation: The negative short answer uses won't.

questions.question: Choose the sentence that expresses a promise.
questions.explanation: I promise explicitly marks the sentence as a promise.

options.text: I will return your book tomorrow, I promise.
I returned your book last month.

questions.question: Complete the immediate decision: The phone is ringing. I ___ answer it.
questions.explanation: Will commonly expresses a decision made at the moment of speaking.

questions.question: Complete: I don't think people ___ stop using the Internet soon.
questions.explanation: After the subject, use will + base verb.

questions.question: Which sentence expresses a prediction?
questions.explanation: A belief about a future result is a prediction.

options.text: Our team has a new coach.
I think our team will win.

questions.question: Choose a polite request using will.
questions.explanation: Will you ... please can be a request.

options.text: You close the door every day.
Will you close the door, please?

questions.question: Complete: We ___ be late; the station is only a minute away.
questions.explanation: Won't is followed by the base form be.

questions.question: Choose the correct future sentence.
questions.explanation: The future existential form is there will be.

options.text: There will be more electric cars.
There are will more electric cars.
There will to be more electric cars.
There wills be more electric cars.
There will are more electric cars.

questions.question: What is the opposite of lend?
questions.explanation: Lend means give temporarily; borrow means receive temporarily.

questions.question: What is the opposite of win?
questions.explanation: Win and lose are opposite results in a competition.

questions.question: What is the opposite of turn on?
questions.explanation: Turn off stops a device operating.

questions.question: What is the opposite of remember?
questions.explanation: Forget means fail to remember.

questions.question: Complete: Please give me ___ my pen when you finish.
questions.explanation: Give back means return something to its owner.

questions.question: Complete: I missed her call, so I will call her ___.
questions.explanation: Call back means return a telephone call.

questions.question: Complete: The shirt is damaged. I am taking it ___ to the shop.
questions.explanation: Take back means return an item.

questions.question: Read: The café is closed now, but it opens again at two. Let's come back then. What does come back mean here?
questions.explanation: Come back means return to the place.

questions.question: Read: I'll lend you £10, but please pay me back on Friday. Who must return the money?
questions.explanation: Pay back means return borrowed money to the lender.

questions.question: A colleague says, “These bags are very heavy.” Which reply uses will to make an immediate offer?
questions.explanation: I’ll carry one for you offers help decided at the moment of speaking.

options.text: Will you be at home tomorrow?
I won’t be in the office next week.
I carry a bag to work every day.

questions.question: Which sentence uses won’t to make a negative prediction?
questions.explanation: Won’t is the negative form of will. Here it expresses a prediction.

options.text: I’m sure the shop won’t open before nine.
Opening times are on the door.
I think the shop will open before nine.
The shop didn’t open before nine yesterday.

questions.question: Choose the opposite action. “Please lower the volume.”
questions.explanation: Raise means increase, the opposite of lower.

questions.question: Complete the phrase. “If this coat doesn’t fit, I’ll take it ___ to the shop.”
questions.explanation: Take it back to the shop means return it to the place it came from.

questions.question: You leave a message because your friend is unavailable. Which sentence asks them to return your phone call?
questions.explanation: Call someone back means return their phone call.

options.text: Could you come back with my book?
Could you write my number down?
Could you turn your phone off this evening?
Could you take this back to the shop?
Could you call me back this evening?

questions.question: Read the conversation. “The forecast says there will be ice tonight.” “Then I’ll take the early bus tomorrow.” Which sentence is a prediction about the weather?
questions.explanation: There will be ice predicts a future condition. The second speaker gives their decision.

options.text: There is a bus stop near here.
I took the bus this morning.
I’ll take the early bus tomorrow.
